definitions.explanation: A handheld optical instrument with two lenses for viewing distant objects, used for birdwatching, sports events, concerts, and stargazing.

examples.japanese: {双眼鏡|そうがんきょう}で{鳥|とり}を{観察|かんさつ}する。
コンサートに{双眼鏡|そうがんきょう}を{持|も}っていった。
examples.english: I brought binoculars to the concert.

examples.japanese: {双眼鏡|そうがんきょう}で{覗|のぞ}くと、{遠|とお}くの{山|やま}の{頂上|ちょうじょう}まで{見|み}えた。
examples.english: When I looked through the binoculars, I could see all the way to the distant mountain peak.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {双眼鏡|そうがんきょう}で{見|み}る (look through binoculars)
- {双眼鏡|そうがんきょう}で{覗|のぞ}く (peer through binoculars)
- {双眼鏡|そうがんきょう}を{構|かま}える (raise binoculars to one's eyes)

USAGE:
The word is composed of {双|そう} (pair), {眼|がん} (eye), and {鏡|きょう} (lens/mirror). For a single-lens telescope, use {望遠鏡|ぼうえんきょう}. In Japan, compact {双眼鏡|そうがんきょう} are especially popular at concerts and theater performances where seats may be far from the stage. Small opera-glass-type binoculars are also called {双眼鏡|そうがんきょう}.
